Baba: Believe it or not Baba shuns the limelight and he has a good nose for a bargain, be it for a car, a bag of drugs or an offshore company.
Baden: Yep, Baden can light a fire and he can put up a tent but he's a pacifist. Hence, if you're out there in the wilderness, starving to death and in need of a big protein hit, don't give the knife to him. He'll kill nothing and only wind up hurting himself.
Baiden: A humble man who works with his hands.
Bailey: The fat happy man that giggles constantly. He works for a merchant bank in downtown New York, London or Sydney and apparently he’s pretty good at what he does. Often seen with spittle on his shirt of a Friday night, all he wants from his life is to hang out with his friends and try to talk to girls.
Bailin: Yep, Bailin was conceived inside a surfboard cover on a cold and chilly night on some beach midway between Sydney and Brisbane, Australia. In adulthood, therefore, you probably can’t blame him that he has more bracelets and necklace-thingos than he’s ever had jobs. However, he walks with a smooth style and he has a cheeky grin, which seems to open more doors than it closes.
Bairdy: It is alleged by chemists, physicists and modern-day philosophers that inside Galaxy Bairdy, the normal laws of Quantum Mechanics do not apply. Indeed, they cannot apply.
Baker: Tough nut. Funny cunt. Good value.
Balin: Balin has a clean heart and is good with his hands. He's uncomfortable in a suit (he hates ties altogether) and he likes girls who wear ornate metal bracelets around their biceps, and who are deeply tanned from places very near the equator. He'd look damn good skin diving in Micronesia, for example, and while many might suggest he do a stint at uni to get him started, all those crowds might suffocate him. Balin, be free!
Balu: He's a funny little bugger, alright. Lot's of friends. Good at building cubby-huts.
BamBam: Yes, I know what you're thinking and no, he isn’t human. Bam Bam is actually the name of a wooden club that has fairy lights wrapped around the outside which strobe on and off. It is owned and used by a famous DJ who pulls it out during the beat-peak of one of his songs when the crowd before him is erupting maximally. Bam Bam loves the noise, he loves the girls screaming at him, and he has no responsibilities in life whatsoever.
Banjo:
Is he a human rights' lawyer?
No.
Is he the pilot of the plane you're travelling on?
No.
Does he shower every day?
No.
Would he pass the rigours of an elite military diving course?
No.
Would he make a lot of people laugh over a quite drink, after he's finished his gig?
Yes. Yes, he would.
Banks: Nope, he'll never work for one and he'll profit quite nicely, both financially and philosophically, from the 4 or 5 or 6 plants he lovingly grows, annually. Banks ain't designed for the city.
Banksy:
The Swedish submarine. (Once upon a time, during war games against an American carrier fleet, the sneaky sub made its way past a ring of destroyers, frigates and cruisers, and nailed the aircraft carrier with a single torpedo, before escaping undetected.)

So, anyone seen him lately?

So, anyone seen him lately?
Bar: Bar is neither sloppy nor stupid. He's the sort of bloke who makes his mind up quickly and rarely changes it. If he says he's going to be somewhere at a given time, that's what will happen.
Barack: The smooth walkin' black man with a big sack. He ain't no hack, so you won't need to watch his back, an' all he really needs is some marines to go on the attack. "Attack who?" you ask. He stops and looks at you evenly, ensures he's got your attention and then says, "Fear. That's what we need to attack.” So be it, Young Barack.
Barnaby: Barnaby loves it when one of his mates has a buck’s party because it means he can try and kiss the strippers.
Barney: The name of any man who owns and runs a pub or a bar, or at least spends three hours every afternoon in the same one as a patron.
Baron:
Option A: The annoying drunkard who is famous at his local night club, if only because he is always the oldest person on the dance floor.

Option B: The staunch loner who deals with his eccentric passion without fanfare or ego.
Barry: Barry is a genial fellow who is rarely rushed and whose heart in the right place
Bart: Basic. Funny guy though and, no, he won't be heading up a major corporation any time soon.
Bartholemew: As a great man once said, talk about a blind man in a dark room trying to find a black cat that isn't there. Bartholemew can barely even put his own trousers on, such is his general level of confusion over just about everything. Nice fellow, however.
Barton:
“Barton!” you yell. “Where are you boy?”

You listen... No, he's not here. Which means he's somewhere else, either fishin', laughin', surfin' or schemin' for girls and maybe a beer.

Barton.
Basil: How can one scientifically describe a beautiful painting? Should we? How? I mean, where do you start, especially if it’s an abstract piece? Take the colours for example…..they’re supposed to be strange and comedic, right?
Bastian: Reasonably forthright and conscientious, Bastian is a traditional man. So traditional, in fact, that he pines for the day when terrorists wipe out the power grid so he will be able to meet and greet foreign and exotic women via the use of an introductory letter that has been written by someone else. (Who knows? Maybe he’s a budding terrorist, himself?)
Bat: Bat has five mobile phones on him. You probably need to ask him why that is, although sometimes in life it's best not to know. Bat.
Baxter: The Curtain Raiser who is actually funnier than the main act.
Bay: An informed man who keeps his opinions to himself, generally. Not mainstream, Bay may very well be a vegan or vegetarian. He’s a nice fellow.
Bayden: You probably wouldn’t make Bayden head of an OH&S consultancy, though he’d fake his way through it and do a good-enough job anyway. What am I talking about, you ask? Well, Bayden is a well-rounded, interesting and interested individual, but he is all about standing up for what you believe in and not shirking your responsibilities, be they personal or professional, and having a laugh, of course. In a nutshell, Bayden as a CEO would do okay, but his company wouldn’t rip any body off ever, and so somewhere sometime profit margins may not be as great as they might be. On the flip side, if every cop was like Bayden new prisons wouldn’t be needed because humour and genuine assistance (at all levels) is what the constabulary would fight all crime with. The results would be staggering. (And in this ‘Bayden World’ naturally, where everyone looks after themselves and everyone else, OH&S consultancies are never needed.)
Bayly: The zombie killer who never leaves home without a handkerchief.
Baz: The ‘zed’ at the end of his name bubbles like French champagne (or cheap beer) and so whoever he is, Baz is effervescent and outgoing in some way, and probably more than most of his peers.
Bealy: The first time you say his name you feel like you’re dealing with a fluffy, jolly kind of cake which wasn’t mixed enough before it went in the oven. Repeat it a few more times and you are confronted with the reality of an extremely well-weighted name and a well-tended personality. When the chips are down Bealy’s gaze turns steely and he moves swiftly and with determination. Courage personified.
Bean: Way deeper than he looks (or sounds), many people surreptitiously seek Bean out for advice because of his streamlined approach to all things.
Bear: Bear only considers he's had a fun night out if he comes home with blood on his shirt and at least one loose tooth. Yes, he's killed people but what the hey. In 4 billion years the sun is going to expand as it dies and engulf the Earth, at which point what will matter?
Beardy: Yes, he has a beard and he is a gifted maniac.
Beau: Beau rhymes with “Oooh!” It is also the name given to the phenomenon of a bag of banana lollies being carried by a 4 year old, who drops the bag, which splits, sending the bananas sprawling through the sand. In anyone’s language this is a tragic event. (Not a natural-born leader.).
Bec: Nope, Bec isn’t a chick, he’s a man with an easy smile and a surprisingly relaxed demeanour. He hardly ever gets into a rage, which is nice, and he has plenty of friends.
Bede:
A single-minded young man who settles on his target displaying neither emotion or fear, whether it's a record sales number for the company he works for, the exit of the 12 foot Tahitian  barrel that he's currently in, or that tiny dot on the map which represents the end to a 400 mile desert crossing.
Does he actually ever work?
…nope.
Beecher: Like a possum preparing for winter, if Beecher sets out to do something he does it, and generally better than any of his peers.
Beef: Beef is not as daft as you might think and he's quite generous with his time and money. His approach to women is basically identical to J.D's - and he has the same deep voice.
Belly: A quiet word here, a gentle nudge of advice there, perhaps a meaningful gift of encouragement anonymously placed on the bonnet when you least expect it. Belly is a team player and will probably go to his grave giving more to the group around him then he would ever expect himself. Better with men than with women.
Ben: Deep in a shallow kind of way, Ben inhabits the role of a loner more than you might think. He may not be the life of the party although he’s not always predictable, either, and he’d definitely suffer at the hands of an interrogator for longer than most.
Benedict:
Option A:  All the girls in the girls' toilets are talking about that Benedict fellow, whose opening line seems to consist of him suggesting that they might like to come home with him and measure his penis. It sounds like Benedict is in for another long, fruitless night.

Option B: Studied law and politics, and if he lines his ducks up right, and he usually does, he'll fight for human rights and maybe one day become the Premier. Go you good thing!
Benj: Benj is one of the most peace-loving animals in the Kingdom. He's been reincarnated many times however, especially in the era of motorcars, because he's thrown himself in front of many in the course of saving a young child from certain death.
Benjamin: Benjamin is a neat, nice and formal individual without being a pain about it, hopefully, and yes, he’s a mild soul that appreciates the good in the world. We can’t all be John Travolta.
Benji: As a North Sea Viking in a past life, Benji is full of Scottish blood and rollicking good humour, although these days he is so nice that even he admits that girls with large bosoms frighten him.
Benn: Like a modern day computer that updates itself automatically, Benn looks after his own affairs with relative ease. The double Ns provide a tall fence behind which we can hear him building, constructing, welding and cavorting. What's he up to in there? No one knows. In fact, here, give us a leg up. Let's take a look...
Benna: Benna’s moral code is extremely rigorous, so much so that he might even evolve into some kind of human rights lawyer. Hard to imagine here, I know, but as a traveller and a peace-lover perhaps it makes sense. He’s a good cook.
Bennett: You know those movies where there is a drinking competition between two people? They're generally surrounded by the whole bar, it's loud, everyone is drunk and it's late, and one man has the job of directing competion and announcing exactly when a shot has been successfully swallowed. He might even  be handling some of the bets. Anyway, that man is Bennett, and while he's a shonky prick he's also good to know.
Benriah: A reincarnated warrior from the moors of middle-England, hundreds of years ago. He was something of a clan leader back then, although he was never that successful. But he planned the battles as well as he could, and if he ever did a past-life regression, today, he would understand why he loves topographic maps as much as he does. Google Earth, therefore, is the most magnificent invention he's ever seen.
Benson: Fast hands. Easy smile. Good with the ladies - and the men if he's in the market for them. Benson is a croupier who is good at making strangers feel at ease.
Bentley: No, he wasn't conceived in the back of one, although the seats would be worth it. Bentley is, however, an erect and diligent man who aspires to the top end of town. Will he get there? No one knows, but his journey will be fun to watch. He's quite the exhibitionist, you know.
Beran: Beran struggles in the kitchen. He loves eating and he loves good food, but cooking is just not his thing. We suspect it's because he has quite a stressful job and when he comes home he just needs to chill out and contemplate nothing.
Beren: No, he's not a sociopath, he’d just comfortable in his own skin and calls a spade a spade. Don’t like it? Leave.
Bernard: As a patron of the arts and a patron of all things related to the delivery of humour and life, Bernard loves champagne and his friends and he’s a marvellous person to have around, but don’t waste his time by asking him to fix your car.
Bernd: A pragmatic man of German or Northern European origin. Once you get a handle on his sense of humour, and let's face it, sometimes that can take years, you will discover he's quite a funny and intelligent individual.
Bernie: Bernie is the sort of man who, at formal functions, will curse at his reflection in the men’s toilet when he realizes that, three minutes earlier, he was chatting-up a girl while he had flecks of food stuck to the side of his chin and an unusual globular shaped mass inside his right nostril.
Bert: Midway between a fart, a burp and a bump in the night, Bert is a light-hearted man who makes everyone feel eminently comfortable – special, even. I wonder where he has gone....
Bertie: Like a goldfish who can only deal with the present moment, Bertie will never own a house and he’ll never be lonely. Funny as fuck, Bertie has a presence that is undeniable.
Bertrand: Bertrand doesn't carry around that many burdens, indeed, he may lug around no baggage whatsoever. He's definitely not a coal miner and as an educated and travelled man, Bertrand remains incredulous at the amount of irrelevant bullshit human beings appear to get involved with. Life should be simple, it should involve laughter and friends and good wine, and interesting stories which force one to consider how fortunate one is: this is his perfect life mantra. (And yes, a tiny wee part of him enjoys being lauded for his unique brilliance, but this isn't unusual.)
Berty: At big luncheons Berty shines. He eats with his hands, talks with a mouthful of food, laughs with unbridled enthusiasm and no matter which vicar is present, and no matter how initially shocked they are at his behaviour, Berty wins them over in the end. He doesn't even realise he's doing it. And at the end of lunch, if the tea is too hot to drink, he'll pour it into the saucer to so it can cool before guzzling it thus.
Bevan: As a close relative of Eugene and Nigel, Bevan is absolutely more energetic and intelligent than one might presume. The great side-effect of the comedy of his name is that he has more friends than most people, and he’s always giving with his time and industrious with his actions.
Bevis: No one is that stupid and obtuse, and Bevis is actually quite delightful. He shrugs his shoulders at most dilemmas and will usually find a way through. Believe it or not he’s quite calm under pressure.
Bhima: A loud leader of his friends who is braver than most. He struggles with shy people and if he doesn’t drive a BMW at some point in his life I’ll eat my hat.
Bickerton:
Ah, Bickerton, where's a camera when you need one? You know those preposterous moments in life when, say, three incredibly unusual events happen at the same time? (eg- you've just finished removing leaves from the roof and you're half way down the ladder with a large screwdriver stuffed down your shorts, when two things happen. 1. You have a sudden attack of diarrhea and 2. There's an earthquake.) Anyway, a moment like this is described in scientific literature as a Bickerton Interception.
No, you can't see them coming. You've just got to do the best you can.
Bill: Sometimes a handshake is all you need to tell you that you like a person. This handshake is known as The Bill. It is a rare and wonderful event.
Billy: Billy perfected his graffiti tag about six months ago and this week, having been given a dare in front of a girl that he really likes, he plans to ride into the city on the top of a train. There’s a 19% chance that he’ll live to tell the tale.
BJ: B.J plays hard (at least he did as a young man), he works hard, he loves his friends and family and he has a very deep sense of what’s wrong and right with the world. And he’ll do what he can to help.
Bjordie: Yep, he's a cocky (and funny) little shit who knows he is good looking. And that's okay. His mother has a list of his addresses and it isn't short, and if anyone kept track of the ladies in his life they might find a similarly thick document. Marketing, advertising and the beach life: this is where you might find him. Has he visited Bondi Beach or Tijuana yet? (If he does he many never leave.)
Blackie: Betwixt between the intellectual world and the soulful realm of the undercurrents, Blackie is sort of bloke who is truly at peace on his surfboard. He’s not an ornithologist, for instance, but he can spot a New Holland Honeyeater quicker than anyone, although, as a trade-off, he carries a whip-like temper and he gets jealous.
Blade: His friends tell the story: Leo, Leon, Tyrone and Jason (Jasonicus thuggus, not Jasonicus raucous.)
Blaine: With all the charisma of a witch's hat Blaine is a self-appointed legend. You certainly can't miss him.
Blair: He’s no bar-room brawler, but Blair is intensely ambitious
Blake: Okay, so he's got another of these American titles that are taking over the world. Fortunately, Blake is a smooth name and so he rides-out all that nonsense with style and with an educated kind of grace. He's actually a lovely fellow who is compassionate and thoughtful, and he's no dill. Not a bad performance all round, to be honest.
Blane: Money, business, money and prestige - seriously brother, who gives a shit. Get out in the desert, get out in the ocean, just get outside anywhere which will peel back your senses and make you feel the blood in your veins. Good luck.
Bligh: Sketchy? Never. Well, as a young fellow it took him a while to find his feet but that happens to most people. He does like his personal projects though and he may never be known as the best Team Player. Very well-suited to city living.
Blowie: "I know, I agree with you, don’t worry. I hate hitting any animal with my car, shit! But we're nearly there, both of us are hungry, and that deer will taste great on the campfire, trust me.”                             -Blowie.
Blue: Shy around girls if he hasn’t got a beer in his hand.
Bo: Deeper than a very shallow pond, Bo rarely bothers with a preamble. He sees it, he’s in. He doesn’t think, he just acts. Bo.
Boab: Okay, so Boab was conceived on a camping trip somewhere between Broome and Darwin, in north-west Australia, which is fine. So, did they send you to school Boab? You do know how to count, right? Indeed, like Murray back in the good old days, Boab feels very uncomfortable around too much traffic, noise and people, so he’s better off staying away from cities. The ocean might do him good as well. He tends to go out with stunning hippy girls with feathers in their hair and sexy leather straps around their biceps.
Boaks: An affable bloke who rarely rushes things and who learns from his mistakes.
Boaz: No not a boab, that’s a tree that gets very big and very old, but Boaz isn’t a bad representation. He’s patient, he likes to do things right, he has a calming demeanour and he has plenty of friends. Not prone to attracting crazy women, Boaz does very well in his own company and in a million years he’d never shop at Ikea.
Bob: Bob is an old ute that’s done about a million miles and he has a fair bit left in him yet. He’s not in mint condition and he’s not meant to be. (Good mates with Graeme.)
Bodhan: In a group of young male idiots who are possessed by the thrill and power of the pack, Bodhan, though not the leader of the group, is the single, shining light who provides a moral compass when needed.
Bodhi: People expect the opposite, and that is exactly why Bodhi is slow to take the initiative. Nice guy though.
Bodo: Bodo loves a good flood. He likes getting out in the waters that are waist deep in his street, and he enjoys helping others in distress. Perhaps it's the idea of boating down the road that he loves? We're not sure.
Boedy: Mate, don’t worry, your parents used to smoke a mountain of weed. Anyway, Boedy is a shy kind of cat who trails behind the corporate leaders who he eventually realises are full of shit. It gives him time to ponder the deeper things in life, anyway, which has also enabled him to realise that beauty is in the small things and therefore everywhere. He’d be an excellent yoga instructor.
Bohden: Bohden has always harboured a desire to go canoeing down a long river with nothing but a tent, some basic provisions and perhaps a gun and a companion/maiden.
Bolthead: Yep, he's the dead-spit of Herman Munster.
Bomber: A giant man with a giant heart. And that's great, but even he would admit to not being the sharpest tool in the box. More than most, Bomber craves a simple life with a loving wife and couple of healthy kids that he can throw around in the back yard in summer time.
Booker: Booker is the kind of bloke who submits a $9 million boat plan to a boat-building company on white butchers’ paper, having spent five minutes drawing it with a black crayon.
Boris: No, there are no surprises here folks. "Now, Boris! Just siddown' otherwise the boat will capsize, you idiot!"
Boston:
You can't choose your family yet, can you? Pity. Anyway, Boston is just a normal, slightly shy kind of fellow.
Will he become the country’s leader?
No way.
Does he have friends?
Yes.
Does he fully believe he can achieve greatness?
Not yet…
Bow: Bow is the only man in the Kingdom that has to charge his jocks. They have weird little LED fairy lights woven into them, you see. He can even alter what they do. Have a chat to him about it - he's not shy at all and he's quite proud of them. He thinks he'll meet a wife because of them.
Bowden: Like solid bark on a healthy old tree, Bowden operates with the minimum of fuss. You will never see him getting married in the nude during a parachute jump, for instance, and everything he does is accomplished with a nonchalant kind of grace. One can easily imagine Bowden’s wife about to enter the water on a SCUBA dive, as part of a resort getaway she had bought them as a treat, and the dive master asking her, “Hang on, you’re on your own. Where’s Bowden?” In all likelihood, she would smile, look back at them and say, “Oh, he’s back at the resort, sitting. Just sitting.”
Bowen: As a professional hunter he's adept as keeping himself in the shadows and he'll quite happily sit hidden in the one spot for hours, if need be.
Bowie: A spender and a pot head.
Boyd: Boyd always looks like he's thinking hard. He's actually quite a funny soul, despite his heavy academic load. Oh, did I mention that Boyd is a geology lecturer at university? Rocks don't move too fast and this suits Boyd to the ground, pardon the pun.
Brad: If he isn’t a new yo-yo (ie. a fad that comes and goes without affecting the philosophy of those that he mingles with) then Brad is a calming soul whose direction in life seems to have been perfectly predestined. It helps that he is almost invariably tall, but in this case, even a short conversation with Brad is enough to provide you with clarity of insight.
Braden: Rarely superficial or flippant, Braden navigates a reasonably meaningful and dedicated path through life. He likes his sport and his girlfriends/lovers/partners etc are normally quite well adjusted.
Bradley: Honestly, does anyone really care? (Note: If this is the only name people know him by, can we suggest that he ignores the career suggestions of his parents by not attending either law or medical school, and that he gets out in the world more than he has? Thanks.)
Brady: Brady is a nice enough guy with plenty of friends and yadda yadda yadda, but he's completely inoffensive.
Brae: He's not Bruce, he's not Ray, he's Brae! Like his cousin Victoria, Brae is a well-mannered horse who knows what-is-what. Unlike horses which are incapable of lying, however, Brae can bend the truth and will often hold his cards very close to his chest. He has plans and he has nous, and why explode with emotion at some unexpected outcome when you know that time is on your side?
Brahm: Man, he's a stubborn prick sometimes. It must be that pig's cranium that sits on top of his neck. But, you have to give him his due because like Sue before him he's wonderful at finishing projects well. He makes an excellent foreman/CEO.
Braith: No, don’t brake Braith, accelerate. Jump. Be daring. Rip off that fucking tie and get out there boy! Who cares what anyone thinks!
Bram: Bram is not the pig-headed mule that you presume he might be. He's actually a little bit shy. He's not a fool, though.
Brandon: Brandon is the branch of a gum tree that broke off in a storm about three years ago. He was sturdy and flexible when he hit the ground but the months in the summer heat have dried him clean and made him frail. Nowadays he’d make easy prey for a hot summer fire that was gathering steam and he’d snap in your hands if you tried to break him in half, but there’s a 20% chance that, if you did that, he would slap you in the face as the final energetic act of his quite complex life.
Brandt: Sure, he does know a lot but can someone take him off the school of human behaviour and teach him the art of reading peoples' reactions? Maybe he just needs to work on his delivery? We know you don't mean to brother, but even if required-information is shoved down peoples' throats you'll end up sitting alone on desert island wondering what happened.
Brant: Brant prides himself on his feet which he pumices regularly. He detests spilt food and messy sex, and he has a spectacularly neat bedroom.
Brantley: Definitely no moron, Brantley is educated and quirky, and it takes more than just a passing shower to dissuade him. He looks like a nerd doesn’t he? He’s not.
Braxton: It's a modern trend apparently, that being when men shave their groin but not their face. Why is that? Yes, Braxton may not indulge in either of these pastimes but he does have all the makings of a rather splendid hipster. It's the hairdo (on his head) that gives it away. Smart guy though, with friends and ability, and as a modern man he's tech savvy, but Lord help us if calamity strikes and suddenly we have no electricity, for the Braxtons will struggle to inherit the earth!
Bray: Rarely prone to dirt and germs, if Bray is travelling then you wont find him in the bug-ridden jungles of Sumatra or Brazil. No, he'll be at a swank resort on either Fiji or Tahiti, sipping cocktails by the pool. The air conditioner in his room is well and truly on.
Brayden: Born into a nice middle-class family, Brayden is good in school, popular with people, successful in life and happy. True, he won’t ever trek to the North Pole, discover a new species of fish in Lake Victoria or get ‘Hi, how are you?’ tattooed down the length of his member, but he’ll procure a wife, have three kids and enjoy watching them grow and contribute, just as he did.
Brec: Many girls have tried to tame Brec for a domestic life inside a house with them, but few have succeeded. Brec is his own man. The five-day stubble isn't a look, he just doesn’t like shaving plus it keeps the sun off. Brec spends more time on his own than most men and he’s fine with that.
Brecken: He can shoot. He can mend a fence. He can remove the testicles of young steers with a knife and he knows how to fix the diff on the Landcruiser. (Note: If he's a city boy he can do none of those things and he spends way too much time in front of the mirror.)
Brekyn: Brekyn rhymes with 'So, waddaya reckon?', even if it's said with a slightly impatient tone. To this end he is a good kid and an industrious young man but he gets bored. And, okay, yes, so he has stubborn horns that stick out the top of his head, but, honestly, who's perfect?
Brendan: Like any sensitive concrete block, Brendan is functional, surprisingly conservative and occasionally highly competitive. And he’s nearly always tall.
Brenden: Like a bashful wee beaver, busy making his little damn in the little creek, he knows people think he's a tiny bit odd. So what if he is? Doesn't Mother Nature have each of us performing strange little deeds that everyone else might think is absurd? This is part of the grand plan, you understand. So, there Brenden is, scurrying around between locations, hiding from the spotlight and sticking to the shade. Predator Avoidance is at the top of his list.
Brendon: A rather dopey bloke who thinks with a clean heart, unless no one is looking.
Brennan: An extremely large and weighty office table made of dark mahogany wood. The rather fantastic item is a place of great insight and, most important, top level secrets….
Brent: Organised. Preoccupied. Occasionally intolerant…or is he? He looks shy but he’s not. He might even be a “player”. I guess we’re about to find out…
Brenton: Brenton, if he is known by this precise name and none other, is about as charismatic and endearing as a dry thicket fence.
Bretnall: An interesting man who never quite got into the party scene, which was a bonus for both his wallet and the amount of highly-functioning grey matter in his head. Having selected a different fork in the road, Bretnall enjoys unusual hobbies and peculiar interests. His ego, thankfully, never really got off the ground and, to be honest, his whole approach is damn refreshing in the modern era. Softly spoken.
Brett: The universal gods were mucking around in the kitchen one day and they put John, Shane and Nathan in a blender and vwa-la: Brett.
Bretto: The Remarkable Clown and another perennial teenager.
Brian:
Option A:  The lemon tree in the back yard that is pissed-on by dogs, men and children. He doesn’t produce tonnes of fruit but he’s growing in excellent soil and it is therefore no effort for him to produce more than enough lemons of the highest quality.

Option B:  Brian is the kind of teacher who, if invited to teach in a mixed race American High School in the 1960s, would create a scandal when, as a white man, he would happily accept the offer to dance from a lovely young black student on prom night. He is also the kind of man who, after rumour got out amongst the parents of the black kids that their teacher was a cool and loving white man, would be invited to attend a large black ball with his wife. On arrival at the ball, he and his wife might even be formerly announced into the room before they realise they are the only white folk present. They might then go on and have one of the nights of their lives. And who knows, maybe the innocent actions of a man like Brian might begin something...
Brie: Yep, Brie is a man, and a gentle, quietly spoken and well-educated man at that. When confronted with the prospect of being conscripted into the army in lieu of some bullshit allied war in the Middle East or somewhere, he will have no compunction in conscientiously objecting. What you may not immediately assume of this fellow is that he is experimental in a very quiet way. (For example, tantric sex is something he'll almost certainly try at, at some point.)
Brighton: Party animal. And sometimes it ain't pretty.
Brin: It’s of constant fascination to his more anal friends how someone can be so late so regularly, yet look so joyously peaceful and happy all the time. Truth is, before he arrived on Earth he made a decision to be friendly and welcoming in all circumstances, and there endeth the lesson. Brin.
Bristle: Bristle is a Commando or SAS soldier and adrenalin is the only thing that makes him tick. On at least one occasion, for example, he has leapt from an aircraft with an Alsatian strapped to his chest.
Brock: Brock would make love to his reflection if he could and he can be extremely impatient.
Brocky: Anoints his own phallus with oil every evening, and whether anyone is watching or not.
Brodie:
What, annoying? Brodie? Well, no, not really. He's too chilled out to be annoying. 
Lazy around the house, maybe, yep.
Popular with his friends and ladies - tick.
Useless at servicing his own car - check.
Well balanced when it comes to dancing/surfing/skating - roger.
And he has a endearing smile and a warm heart. That's our Brodie for you.
Brody: Brody the Show Pony. For employment he works as a bell on a little girl’s new bicycle, unless he’s the Brody that cuts down trees for a living, in which case he’s far more elemental and genuine – good value, as a matter of fact.
Brogan: Now, Brogan, you're never going to change the world if you cannot, for the life of you, remember to take your shoes off!
Brogue: Brogue loves the modern trend of brushing your fringe diagonally across your face that covers your eyes completely, as it means he doesn’t have to look directly at anyone. No, he's not an arrogant twat, he's just a little vein. He'll grow out of it.
Bronco: Bronco has no pain receptors in his brain, what so ever.
Bronson:
Here we have the tidings from another mother obsessed with another Hollywood star. What do you do? But, old Bronson here is far deeper than these mere trifles. He thinks about it, he looks at the bigger picture, he takes a moment to reflect and he judges reasonably well, most of the time. Yes, he has friends and admirers and he'll go places if he wants because his ego works with him, not against him.

(Just dont tell him we said all that.)
Brook: Brook is an even-tempered player who stays within the limits of the stadium. He might get a friend to place a bet on the game in which he's playing, but that's about as daring as he'd get, although if the sporting body found out he'd be in trouble. Not bad with the ladies.
Brooklyn: Brooklyn, hear this: A couple of hard day’s work won't kill you. It might even be good for you.
Brooksy: The Camel. He’s his own man, he hardly ever feels the need to rush, he sleeps whenever the need takes him, and for as long as he likes, and if he’s feeling social he is excellent company.
Broughton:
Broughton brings a fair thwack to the table. 
He brings integrity (when he’s not lying to his girlfriend about stuffing $50 notes down the front of a stripper’s G-string), he brings an educated background (despite an on-going issue with alcohol he graduated, almost with Honours), and he brings a large group of dedicated friends (who are mostly male, in lieu of a reasonably male-led life).
Most of all, and for all intent and purposes, Broughton is friendly and he has a kind heart (so we suggest that 66.6% of the time, when you read his name theory, please omit all that is enclosed in brackets).

Browny: Like an exposed Kimberley escarpment that is 200 million years old, in Northern Australia, Browny is true to the bone.
Bruce: Bruce rhymes with Clunk. As an anvil in an iron monger’s workshop, Bruce has been whacked and hammered with all forms of hammers and mallets but he’s up to it. It gives him something to belt his head against, and there’s no harder crunching in the world than metal banging against metal. Some smiles are just impossible to remove.
Brucey:
The joker of the group who, even amid some earth-shattering catastrophe, will find something to smile about. He loves it when his wife calls him Brucey because it almost invariably means he’s in for a bit of nookie that night, at which point he smiles to himself, punches the air and whispers, “Go Brucey! You little ripper!” 
Brucey is hard not to love, no matter how well you know him.
Bruno: Bruno, we’re trying to sleep here so can you just shut-up?
Brutus: Remarkable for not only his size and strength, Brutus is famous because he can be easily convinced that, by placing each foot in a metal pale and gripping the respective handles in each hand, if he tries hard enough, he can actually lift himself off the ground.
Bryan: Heavens to Betsy, how many times has Bryan had to remind people of the spelling of his name? Oddly enough this very process has aided Bryan to become something of a solemn, peace-filled and quietly-spoken sage. Bryan has a sense of humour which is never overt (he’s no exhibitionist) and believe it or not he is quite artistic. (And yes, more so than his rather rural twin brother, Brian.)
Bryant: Slightly left of centre, Bryant apsires to study English literature at a prestigious university. Yes, it's true, he's always had a crush on Audrey, but he needs to buck-up if he wants to keep up with her. He doesn't have a clue what he'll do with his degree, however. Indeed, that's a good question. Lad, what's the plan?
Bryce: If the day comes when the American President has to get on the TV and tell the world of a meteor that has been discovered hurtling through the universe on a trajectory that will make it catastrophically collide with Earth, then he or she will read from a prepared statement that those in the White House know of as the Bryce Statement. It will be well articulated and perfectly presented with emotion, compassion and hopefully a drop of humour, but in the end it’s all about telling us how we are going to die. It’s probably a nice way to be told, truth be known.
Brycie: You grin when you say his name and you therefore smirk when you think of him, so it’s probably a given that you laugh and be grateful in his company. Brycie is a cracking bastard, all round.
Bryden: If you get him drunk enough he'll show you, for Bryden is very proud of his titanium cock ring.
Bryn: Bryn is a cross between a grin, a surfboard fin and a big fat bunger as rolled by a happy hippy.
Brynley: Brynley married Hilary and, while they'd never admit it, they fornicate about six times every four years.
Bryson:
You peer down at the river from on top of the bridge, wondering if you haven’t bitten off more than you can chew. You rub your chin thoughtfully in contemplation of the consequences. You're pretty sure there aren't any hidden snags, you don't think it's so far to fall that if you muff the entry you'll be unable to get back to the surface because of a possible injury, but you're not sure. So, yes, I'm going to jump, you think, and that's fine.
But the tiny crook of a frown that forms between your eyes while you're thinking about all of this is called, the Bryson Quirk. And it's healthy.
Bud: No, he's not a beer but sometimes you wonder, although he's not as lazy you might think. He's actually quite an astute little businessman.
Buddha: Buddha is lucid and completely real.
Buddy: Dangerous and brilliant, Buddy is the mercurial wonder child. Let’s just pray he never gets to grow up....
Buggy: Like a frustrated Border collie who wished that his owner would just throw the fucking ball, Buggy is fun-loving, highly intelligent and direct.
Bullfrog: Bullfrog has big red chubby cheeks and probably carries the tattoo of a lily on the point of his shoulder.
Bumhead: A bit thin on top, and hopefully only literally.
Bunk: The country bumpkin whose gun collection is worth thousands. He knows how to use them too. He also spends more time at the pub than he does at home, although he does enjoy drinking and shooting at the same time.
Burchell:
Employment consultant, or some such administrative position is where you'll find this fellow. Burchell, a wee word of warning: if we up here in the commentary box are ever taxed for breathing oxygen, then we are coming to hunt you down. True story. We urge you to bare this in mind. 

Ever heard of Burning Man?....you should go.
Burkey: Burkey is the kind of bloke who loses his underwater camera after nearly drowning in a pearl-diving accident. Three months later, within a kilometre or two from where he thought he's nearly died, he's also the kind of bloke to spot a strange barnacle-encrusted rock that looks abit odd, before recognising it as his underwater housing. (Camera dry as a bone and intact.) Last I heard he and his partner gave birth to a daughter who was also so into life that, even on Day 1, she couldn't be left alone in a room because she kept dragging herself out of it. Which newborn does that? Burkey.
Bus: His name says it all. He sports a large welcoming personality and he loves to travel, although if he stays in one place for too long grass tends to grow-up around his wheels and he ends up never leaving.
Bushy: It matters not that he’s had no formal training. Bushy is the outback mechanic, and he knows his shit.
Buster: Buster is almost impossible to tell-off because he always has a believable and convincing excuse at the ready. He's never malicious in his response - he's too friendly a guy for that. But he's smooth and a bit slick. Girls take ages to trust him.
Butch: Butch is a funny guy and he has plenty of irreverent friends but, even if he's doing it as a joke, he'd  never step into a straight-jacket without a knife hidden in his hand. Best mates with Marco.
Byron:
Byron loves cooking and you should see him go. He starts preparing the day before by washing and ironing his white chefs apron, even though he's not a chef, classically speaking. He also likes to wear a tall chef's hat even if he's cooking for just himself. Why does he do this? I'm not sure. Is it perhaps because he has a flair for the dramatic?

Perhaps.
